Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Is the challenge to match the Quran a fair test?

The Quran invites doubters to answer in kind. Who could judge it, and what can a reader of translation test?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down [i.e., the Qur’ān] upon Our Servant [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)], then produce a sūrah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses [i.e., supporters] other than Allāh, if you should be truthful.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:23

Most books ask to be believed. This one says something else about itself: if you are in doubt, answer it. Bring a single chapter like it, and bring any helper you wish. Look at what that does. It hands the reader a test and puts the book itself at risk, because a claim that can be tried is a claim that can fail. Whether it fails is what the next parts look at.

A question for you

When a source says ‘test me’, what is your first reaction?

If you sayInterest. Let me see.
ThenThen the test is yours to run. What follows shows what running it involves, and where it is hard.
If you saySuspicion. There must be a catch.
ThenA fair suspicion. There are real catches, and the next part names them: who judges, and what a reader of translation can test.
If you sayIt depends who judges.
ThenThat is the sharpest question here, and the next part takes it up.

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ ۖ قُلْ فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or do they say [about the Prophet (ﷺ)], "He invented it?" Say, "Then bring forth a sūrah like it and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allāh, if you should be truthful."

Quran · Yunus 10:38

﴿قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجْتَمَعَتِ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتُوا۟ بِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِۦ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur’ān, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants."

Quran · Al-Isra 17:88

Two things are said here. The ask is small: one chapter. And a forecast is added: even if people and jinn joined forces, they would not bring its like. A forecast is a risk the book takes in public. But a risk is only real if someone can judge the result, and there is no neutral referee for ‘like it’. Anyone honest has to say that first.

A question for you

Whom would you trust to judge whether something is ‘like’ a text?

If you sayPeople who know the language deeply.
ThenThen the arguments of scholars of Arabic are the ones to read, including their disagreements with one another.
If you sayOrdinary readers, over centuries.
ThenA fair standard too. It asks what lasts and what people return to, not what a panel approves.
If you sayNo one can.
ThenThat is an honest position, and close to the objection scholars themselves record. It does not stop you listening for yourself, which is next.

Part 3 of 3

﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُۥ ۚ بَل لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ٣٣ فَلْيَأْتُوا۟ بِحَدِيثٍ مِّثْلِهِۦٓ إِن كَانُوا۟ صَـٰدِقِينَ٣٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or do they say, "He has made it up"? Rather, they do not believe. Then let them produce a statement like it, if they should be truthful.

Quran · At-Tur 52:33-34

Here is the hard part for readers in translation. Much of the test is about the Arabic: its sound, its rhythm, how its words are arranged. A translation carries the meaning, not that. Anyone who says you can see it in English is overselling. What you can do is listen to a recitation and let your own ear judge. Nobody can do that part for you.

A question for you

What would you like to do with this part?

If you sayListen to a recitation, with the meaning beside it.
ThenMany readers begin with one short chapter, heard once without reading. Let the ear go first and the meaning follow.
If you sayRead what scholars of Arabic have argued, and what critics say.
ThenThat is where the tradition's own case lives, and the objections to it. Neither is hidden.
If you saySet this test aside.
ThenThat is fine. It is one sign among several, and the others do not depend on Arabic.

Your reflection

What is the best thing you have read that you could not have written, and how did you know?
